evidence_frontier: Recent experiments show that local widths 8 and 12 both passed the preregistered gate (candidate_correct >= control_correct -10) on fresh seed sets (w8: 444≥448-10, w12: 445≥453-10). The w8 100‑epoch confirmation used seeds [42,43,44,45,46] and w12 100‑epoch confirmation used seeds [101,102,103,104,105]. Both used ECG200, 100 epochs, and 500 predictions per model. These results establish that compression to width 8 is viable and that width 12 is robust, but the performance curve between these widths remains uncharacterized.
analysis: Observation: Widths 8 and 12 each meet the relative performance gate against the width‑16 control under independent seed sets. Observation: No experiment has evaluated an intermediate width such as 10 with the same confirmation protocol. Hypothesis: Width 10 will also satisfy the gate, indicating a monotonic relationship between local width and Q.ANT correctness within the tested range.
hypothesis: When trained for 100 epochs on ECG200 with a fresh set of five seeds, the candidate model with local_width=10 will achieve aggregate Q.ANT correct at least (control_correct -10), i.e., candidate_correct >= width16_control_correct -10.

proposal.title: 100‑epoch Width‑10 Confirmation on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Does an intermediate local width of 10 retain the required performance relative to the width‑16 control under a fresh seed set?
proposal.rationale: Testing width 10 fills the gap between the already confirmed widths 8 and 12, allowing us to map the width‑performance trade‑off and assess whether compression benefits continue smoothly. This informs future architecture scaling decisions without assuming minimal viable width.
proposal.risks: Width 10 may fail the gate, limiting compression expectations; seed selection could unintentionally favor one model; simulation results do not translate to physical hardware performance.
